title: Sensory Circuit
strapline: Alert, organise, calm — a short movement journey that helps a wound-up or under-powered body find its 'ready to learn' setting.
intent: Children whose bodies are over- or under-aroused get the movement input they need to reach a calm, alert state.
Children learn what their own body needs — big movement to wake up, deep pressure to settle — and start to seek it out.
Children build core strength, balance and coordination through purposeful, sequenced physical challenge.
Children experience a reliable ritual that bookends busy times, easing tricky transitions like arrival or pre-group.
Children develop body awareness and self-regulation they can eventually run for themselves.
implementation: Build three phases: alerting (bouncing, jumping, spinning), organising (balancing, crawling, target-throwing), then calming (pushing, pulling, deep pressure, slow stretches).
Always finish on the calming phase so children leave settled, not revved — the order is the whole point.
Keep it short and frequent — five to ten minutes before a demanding part of the day beats a long session once a week.
Offer heavy work that grounds: pushing a weighted trolley, carrying the crate of blocks, wall press-ups, a bear-hug squeeze.
Watch each child and adjust the dose — some need more alerting, some go straight to calming — and note what works for whom.
Run it warmly and playfully as a movement adventure, never as therapy done to a child.
key_questions: How does your body feel — wriggly, sleepy, or just right?
What movement do you think would help right now?
Can you feel the squeeze in your arms when you push?
Which part of the circuit is your favourite?
Are you ready and calm now, or do you need one more go?

impact.text: Children run, climb, balance, jump and crawl with growing confidence and control.
Children negotiate space and obstacles well and control their whole-body movement.
Children begin to know what their body needs — movement, rest, calm — and do something about it.
Children regulate big feelings using strategies that work for them, with adults nearby not in charge.
Children shift attention and settle into group times more readily after organising movement.

enhancements: A photo sequence of the circuit stations so children can follow and eventually lead the order themselves.
A weighted-blanket or bean-bag squeeze station for the calming phase for children who crave deep pressure.
An outdoor version using logs to balance, a hill to roll down and a wall for press-ups.
A 'body engine' visual — too slow, too fast, just right — to talk about arousal in language little ones grasp.
Calming-phase music that's slow and steady, cueing the wind-down every time.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into bouncing, spinning and climbing for the sheer physical joy of it.
The circuit invites children to test what their body can do at each station.
active_learning: Children come back to the movements that make them feel 'just right', learning to seek regulation.
Persisting through the balance and heavy-work stations builds strength and a sense of achievement.
creating_thinking: Children begin to connect how their body feels with what it needs and choose accordingly.
They notice the calming effect and start to self-prescribe a squeeze or a push when wound up.
